verdict.tagline: Brutal survival hiding technical friction behind a steep learning curve.
for_you_if: you enjoy harsh survival mechanics without handholding
you can handle steep crafting learning curves
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance during the tutorial
you want reliable cooperative multiplayer saves
you experience motion sickness from camera effects

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks settings to disable motion blur or fish-eye lens effects, causing motion sickness and disorientation.

citations.review_text: ZERO options to adjust or turn off the overdone motion blur. The launch option no longer works in 2026. All motion-sick people, AVOID.

I may not have much time into this game, but there is a very good reason. Motion Blur. The game is disorienting for people that can get motion sick easy. I did not make it through the tutorial, and neither did my friends. This wouldn't be a problem if there was an option to turn it off, but alas, there is not. So, eventually my friends and I hung it up before our survival even began, 

This game seemed interesting. Tedious, most definitely, but that is something I could have gotten used to. Should the developers ever add a setting to turn off motion blur maybe I'll return. Until then, I will likely not install again.

Nope. Forced Fisheye lense - I'm about 2 mins into the tutorial and my first reaction is: wtf is this? Turning around makes me feel sick, everything is warped to hell. I google it, there's posts all over the place talking about it and a mod which removes it. So needed to mod the game after 2 mins in. Next, the tutorial doesnt update its key bind references, so I'm beign told to press the wrong button on both tutorial steps and on tool tips in the back pack. Nope. Game uninstalled. Seriously WTF. Its not hard to mess this up.

For who has problem with game motion sickness or motion blur sickness, slightly or seriously, this game has it, i dont have trouble play fps with moving or shaking screen like dying light or else but man i feel soooo dizzyy to play this, i cant continue to play after 30mins with every object moving spinning around whenever i look around

claims.claim: Reviewers experience crashes during or immediately after completing the tutorial sequence.

citations.review_text: always crashing and bad tutorial

The true hell is the tutorial, otherwise it seems fine. Game crashed at end of tutorial. Tried launching a single player game. Starts with the tutorial content.... went to leave because i couldn't do it twice. I couldn't bare it. Then i saw the beautiful button. "skip tutorial". Then i could play the game for real.

I really wanted to like this game. I did. But I was not capable of liking the game. Skill issue, I know.

The game has a tutorial, which I appreciate. After completing it, the game crashed. But I had completed it, so it was time to start the game proper, which begins with the tutorial. What? Why? So I completed it a second time upon which it crashed a second time. The third time I loaded in right at the end of the tutorial where it crashed a third time. And finally I loaded in the fourth time and paused where I found the "skip tutorial" option. Taking it I managed to get to the "first area".

Here, the game announces that the water is unsafe. Sounds like I need to get a fire going, but to do that I need sticks. Can I pick up sticks? No... sticks don't grow on trees... they must be cut down with an axe that requires a stone. Can I use this stone? NO!!! that's a big stone, and that won't work. Can I hit big stones with other big stones to break them into smaller stones? NO!!! that... wasn't thought of by us, so you can't. okay, well here's a bunch of water, surely there's  a stone in there? NO!!! this water has nothing but ground decorated to look like stones. No actual stones. 

Well what am I supposed to do? Find a stone, obviously. Okay So should I move to this next area? NO!!! You're way too under equipped for that. I guess I'll sleep then? NO!!! That lowers your sanity. Now the game is screaming at me that I'm not good enough. So I literally turn off the sound to block out how annoying the game is. After searching the entire area and finding one single stone... in a jungle... in a river... I made an axe that held up like tissue paper. When it broke I got the instructions for a bigger axe. Neither axe can open the coconut. I'm dying of thirst, have to mute the game. And still can't make more stones. Still can't survive the next area... I just...

It's pretty clear that the emphasis on difficulty took priority over fun. And if you're going to say "Well, I had fun".…

This is hands down the worst game I've ever played. No competition. The tutorial is absolutely terrible. I spent forever just trying to figure out the basic controls and mechanics because the game explains almost nothing properly. And after finally getting through that nightmare, the game crushed. Seriously？What makes it even worse is that the entire tutorial had to be done again from the beginning. How can a game with optimization this bad even be released? This feels unfinished and completely untested!!!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that controller input fails to work properly, featuring invisible virtual mouse cursors or a complete lack of controller detection.

citations.review_text: game does not work on controller. cant get past the crafting tutorial as selecting items gives some weird virtual mouse u have to control with the joystick, but its completely invisible as well as appearing to have insanely low sensitivity. unplayable and will refund

Unfortunately, I can't say with one way or the other if Green Hell is or is not worth playing or not this is due to the fact that the game refuses to either detect my controller or doesn't have any control compatibility at all. And I've tried ALL the troubleshooting options; putting Steam in The Big Picture Mode, unplugging and replugging my controller back in, and restarting my PC. Heck I did the last two things three different times and still the game would not detect my gamepad. So unless either the developers or somebody is able to assist with figuring out why my controller isn't being detected in game and resolving it, I'll have essentially just flushed $3 down the toilet. But that's no big whoop. What is kind of a big deal is but I also paid for StarRupture, and at the moment of writing this review I am downloading it, and I'm hoping like hell that game doesn't have the same issue with controller compatibility as Green Hell does...

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the tutorial fails to explain basic mechanics and controls, requiring external guides or internet searches to figure out actions like starting a fire or crafting items.

citations.review_text:
it might be a good game, but this game disrespects the time of the player, but giving absolutely no information on how to use the interface.
Like normally u would think about what do u need to do to survive - that that is what a survival game should be about. Here u get a task right in the tutorial: craft a hand drill, where u already know how it works irl, but u need to look it up on the internet, because there is absolutely no information on what to do to "craft" the same thing in the game.
If the tutorial is like that and there is no save feature whatsoever, I wont have the patience as the player to manage the different status bars, while spending most of my time trying to figure out what the game allows me to use and what I have to do on the interface to actually make them work.

30 MINUTES OF 'PLAYING' just to realize the tutorial doesn't actually teach you anything and I can't even make a fire...And I guess that means no refund. You shouldn't have to google how to get through a tutorial!!! What a chit game, don't waste your money.

Looks fun but the controls are different than all other survival games making it extremely difficult to figure how what to do and when to do it. When I had to google how to build a fire as one of the first things in order to build one. That's not a good sign.

Can't believe I'm leaving a bad review on a game i got for $3 and only played for 30 minutes, but I only played for 30 minutes for a reason.  

Starting the game for the first time, I decide to play the tutorial to learn the basics of the crafting.  5 minutes into the tutorial and I've learned nothing but how to activate the walkie talkie to listen to endless story babble.  I thought this was a tutorial, not the story mode.

So I decide to leave the tutorial, and also skip story mode on account of the endless babble of the tutorial, and go straight to winging it in survival.  I begin with a notebook full of crafting recipes, but none for simple basics like a spear or stone axe.  I'm also finding sticks everywhere and soon fill my backpack, but there is little to craft with them.  I fear I might need to do the tutorial after all.

Now I'm back in the tutorial, and I've sat through all the tripe again to finally get to the instruction on how to build a fire.  6 sticks, no problem.  Or is it?  After searching the tutorial area for several minutes and finding only 1 stick (was literally finding them under every tree in survival mode), I exited the game and came here to complain.  Not a great first impression of the game.  I will probably give it another try at some point, using the internet as my tutorial, but omg I won't sit through that tutorial babble again.

I've only completed the tutorial so far, but I'm already enjoying the game. The survival mechanics, graphics, and crafting system all feel realistic and well made.

My biggest issue is the tutorial. It isn't detailed enough and doesn't clearly explain what you're supposed to do. A more guided, step-by-step introduction would make it much easier for new players to learn the basics. For example, instead of simply telling players to craft an item, it should explain where to find the required materials and how to combine them.

I'm refunding the game, but not because it's bad. I just don't enjoy playing survival games alone, and I don't think I'll be able to find anyone to play with. My friend also decided not to continue because they found the tutorial too confusing and difficult to follow. I think improving the tutorial would make a much better first impression and help more new players stick with the game.

dont even bother playing the tutorial it doesnt teach you anything i spent a good 30 minutes trying to figure out how to light a campfire IN THE TUTORIAL after finally figuring it out i realized how stupid it is

Cannot learn to start a fire, the tutorial is not explaining how to do what it wants you to do. What's the point of a tutorial if its not going to teach you how to use the buttons or keypad to do what you need to do. Got very bored with it very quick. Not interesting or fun when you cannot figure out why the same actions on youtube videos are not working for you. Maybe a bug or something. Either way I'm just glad I brought for dirt cheap (90% off) otherwise I would call it a rip off. Do NOT get this game unless you want to invest in a lot of your time figuring out how to learn the controls etc. because the game does not teach you that..

there are waaaaay to many good reviews forgiving a game with no real way of how to learn anything without internet resources because the devs didnt even do a tutorial and the system is completly crap for figuring things out


 TERRIBLE GAME DONT BUY
The user interface is beyond abstruse. I had to google for help three times to complete the second task in the tutorial. You know, the part of the game that is supposed to teach you how to play.

This is hands down the worst game I've ever played. No competition. The tutorial is absolutely terrible. I spent forever just trying to figure out the basic controls and mechanics because the game explains almost nothing properly. And after finally getting through that nightmare, the game crushed. Seriously？What makes it even worse is that the entire tutorial had to be done again from the beginning. How can a game with optimization this bad even be released? This feels unfinished and completely untested!!!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that finishing the tutorial restarts the intro story sequence instead of progressing smoothly into the main game.

citations.review_text: The true hell is the tutorial, otherwise it seems fine. Game crashed at end of tutorial. Tried launching a single player game. Starts with the tutorial content.... went to leave because i couldn't do it twice. I couldn't bare it. Then i saw the beautiful button. "skip tutorial". Then i could play the game for real.

I really wanted to like this game. I did. But I was not capable of liking the game. Skill issue, I know.

The game has a tutorial, which I appreciate. After completing it, the game crashed. But I had completed it, so it was time to start the game proper, which begins with the tutorial. What? Why? So I completed it a second time upon which it crashed a second time. The third time I loaded in right at the end of the tutorial where it crashed a third time. And finally I loaded in the fourth time and paused where I found the "skip tutorial" option. Taking it I managed to get to the "first area".

Here, the game announces that the water is unsafe. Sounds like I need to get a fire going, but to do that I need sticks. Can I pick up sticks? No... sticks don't grow on trees... they must be cut down with an axe that requires a stone. Can I use this stone? NO!!! that's a big stone, and that won't work. Can I hit big stones with other big stones to break them into smaller stones? NO!!! that... wasn't thought of by us, so you can't. okay, well here's a bunch of water, surely there's  a stone in there? NO!!! this water has nothing but ground decorated to look like stones. No actual stones. 

Well what am I supposed to do? Find a stone, obviously. Okay So should I move to this next area? NO!!! You're way too under equipped for that. I guess I'll sleep then? NO!!! That lowers your sanity. Now the game is screaming at me that I'm not good enough. So I literally turn off the sound to block out how annoying the game is. After searching the entire area and finding one single stone... in a jungle... in a river... I made an axe that held up like tissue paper. When it broke I got the instructions for a bigger axe. Neither axe can open the coconut. I'm dying of thirst, have to mute the game. And still can't make more stones. Still can't survive the next area... I just...

It's pretty clear that the emphasis on difficulty took priority over fun. And if you're going to say "Well, I had fun".…

The game overcomplicates things that should be and need to be simple. Something as simple as starting a fire (not really simple IRL i get it) has you pressing too many buttons and opening too many tabs. Just for a fire. Inspecting each limb is also something Creepy Jar thought would be a really cool and impressive mechanic. It might be, but not in my case. For some people, it is nothing but unnecessary and annoying. This game could have been much better if it wasn't for the overcomplication of simple and base game features. 

There are too many buttons to remember, too many things to do with those buttons. Even the tutorial itself was kind of hard to follow because it's trying to (albeit decently) explain a whole bunch of overcomplicated game mechanics that don't need to be there. 

Additionally, the tutorial itself is nothing but the intro to the game coupled with textual instructions. Moreover, when you complete the tutorial, you are sent back to the option in the menu to play single or multiplayer. In my case, i selected singleplayer and it started the entire story alongside the intro part (30 mins part) ALL OVER AGAIN.

Talking about the graphics, they are decent. i do not care much about graphics, but if i have to comment, they can be a bit better for a game released in 2019. 

I came with high hopes that this might be a good rival to SOTF, but i left in disappointment.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the backpack has a weight limit that easily gets overloaded, resulting in a slow walking penalty.

citations.review_text: This is an amasing game, at the begining you might panic about stuff, and maybe die a lot, but that is a learning curve that needs to be done, with enough practise, you can survive easily, by just preparing enough, and knowing what to do in certain situations, I really would recomend this game. The only complaint I have with this game is that the backpack system has an weight limit that can, at least for me, easily be overdone, and the penalty for that is walking very slow.

[h1]Survival Means Suffering[/h1]

[b]Graphics & Visuals: 8.5/10[/b]
[i]Green Hell isn't trying to impress you with cutting-edge graphics. Instead, it focuses on building a believable rainforest, and it succeeds. Dense vegetation, convincing lighting, natural color grading, and excellent environmental detail make the Amazon feel alive without looking artificial. Even years after release, the visuals have aged gracefully. More importantly, after a few hours you stop paying attention to the graphics entirely because the world itself becomes believable enough to pull you in.[/i]

[b]Gameplay & Survival Mechanics: 9/10[/b]
[i]This is where Green Hell separates itself from most survival games. Hunger and thirst are only the beginning. You constantly inspect your body for cuts, parasites, infections, leeches, venom, broken bones, and other injuries. Healing isn't as simple as pressing a medkit button. You actually clean wounds, apply the correct bandages, remove parasites by hand, and prepare natural medicine from plants you discover in the jungle. The crafting system is deep, logical, and rewarding, although gathering materials can sometimes become exhausting. At times the game arguably pushes realism too far, making your character feel more fragile than an average human realistically would be, but that brutality is also part of its identity.[/i]

[b]Crafting & Progression: 9/10[/b]
[i]Crafting is one of Green Hell's strongest features. Almost everything is built manually through experimentation or by recording discoveries in your survival notebook. Weapons, shelters, traps, tools, medicines, fires, food preparation, and defensive structures all require planning rather than simple menu crafting. Progression isn't driven by traditional RPG levels. Instead, your survival skills naturally improve through repeated use, encouraging learning over grinding and making every successful expedition feel earned.[/i]

[b]Story: 8.5/10[/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking tutorials or handholding, requiring players to learn mechanics and recipes through trial and error or external guides.

citations.review_text: Green Hell is one of the most brutal, immersive, and rewarding survival games on Steam. If you think games like The Forest or Rust are tough, this game will give you a serious reality check. It does not hold your hand.
Very difficult game without guides, besides that it's an amazing experience to play this game (I recommend playing with a friend)

"Green Hell," developed and published by Creepy Jar, is a brutally immersive and unforgiving open-world survival simulator that drops you into the dense, treacherous Amazon rainforest. Stripping away most modern conveniences, the game challenges you to manage not only your basic needs—hunger, thirst, and stamina—but also your mental state, as the isolation and constant threats of the jungle begin to wear down your sanity.

The game's greatest strength is its relentless commitment to realism and immersion. The jungle is a stunningly detailed and deadly ecosystem, where every snake bite, infected wound, or careless step can spiral into a life-or-death situation. The layered health and injury system is particularly impressive, requiring you to diagnose and treat specific ailments with limited resources. However, this uncompromising realism comes at a cost; the steep learning curve and punishing mechanics can feel overwhelming and frustrating, especially in the early hours. Additionally, the narrative, while intriguing, often feels secondary to the sheer struggle for survival.

Pros:

-Unmatched commitment to realistic and immersive survival mechanics, including a detailed injury and sanity system.
-Stunningly beautiful and authentically dangerous rainforest environment.
-A satisfying progression from helpless survivor to skilled jungle inhabitant.

Cons:

-Brutally steep learning curve that can be punishing and discouraging for new players.
-The story, while interesting, often takes a backseat to the relentless survival demands.
-Some crafting recipes and item interactions can feel unintuitive without external guides.

Overall, "Green Hell" is a masterclass in hardcore survival simulation, perfectly suited for players who crave authenticity and challenge above all else. While its unforgiving nature and steep learning curve will not appeal to everyone, those willing to embrace its harsh realities will find a deeply rewarding and genuinely tense survival …

It's DIRT CHEAP for how good the game is. 
it's like old stuff with little to no guide and you just learn by dying...dying A LOT 
but it's quite a good survival! specially if you got some buddies to co-op with. 
base building the more you progress in the game the less important it feels since you really need to move around and you rarely come back to certain parts.

Also a small tip for anyone starting this game , take screenshooots of the initial sheets you will see , when you're extremely stuck in a specific situation check those

super reccomended specially by how cheap its when its on sale!

Great survival game that is weighed down by lackluster exploration and annoying glitches. A 7/10.

The survival aspect of the game is amazing when compared to most within this genre. This game does almost no handholding, except for ailments when you get them meaning your probably already dead. This game's tutorial gives the tried and true "uncle and 6-month old swimming lesson" by throwing you in and watching you drown as very important mechanics and ways of interact with the environment will be not introduced. Majority of your first few hours will be experimenting with plants, the crafting menu, and statuses to hopefully avoid death. Figuring out recipes and various important processes feels satisfying and fairly intuitive/realistic for the setting. Survival does become very easy, even on Green Hell, once you understand fundamental crafting recipes, what satisfies certain macros, and cures to ailments. Only real complaint is that some processes are restricted to what the game allows, so its a little difficult, but not impossible, to naturally find the solution at first start. For example I known I need to boil water, but what steps does the game expect me to do? [spoiler] Instead of picking up a bowl I dipped in river and moving it to a campfire, its getting both an enclosed container and a bowl as you need to fill the enclosed container with water by moving it from your inventory into the river then moving the container into the bowl which needs to be next to a campfire [/spoiler]. The UI can feel fairly clunky, especially when attempt to drag backpack items into the environment or vice versa. The Inspect body mechanic is very cool, but it usually does just end up being a 15 second process of removing leeches every 5 minutes. 

The exploration was the weakest element to me. Without a doubt this game looks great, however exploration didn't seem to provide a propose beyond advancing the story/DLC or seeing a "semi-new" environment. Majority of the time it really nev…

Still crashes on me all the time, which is a bit of a shame for a title that has been out of early access for so long. Combine that with a lack of auto save features and you got yourself a ruined evening. 

The game is fun when it doesn't though,
...although it's pretty punishing if you don't know already what you're doing. It's supposed to be "realistically hard", and in some ways it succeeds with that while failing in others. The game teaches you its mechanics very clumsily through failure and the PC's voice lines. If you're playing with a group of newbies that works best imo, you just keep failing and eventually figure ♥♥♥♥ out. 
If you're playing alone or you're the only new guy you should either be tolerant to frustration or not mind looking some things up. 

Either way, it was fun for me (mainly because of the gut punch of a story), but I'll not come back. The crashes are just too annoying imo. 

(Playing on Windows 11, Ryzen 7000 series CPU, RX 7000 series GPU, tons of RAM. This is not my PC's fault.)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the map lacks a player position indicator, making navigation and exploration difficult without landmarks or outside maps.

citations.review_text:
Green Hell is a fantastic survival game with an Interesting storyline.

Suggestion: It would be really helpful if the map showed a marker indicating the player's current location. It's very easy to get lost in the jungle, especially for new players. Once you become familiar with the map, though, exploring and progressing through the game becomes a lot more fun.

wow, just freaking amazing, what a ride. i shot logs in the head thinking they were alligators, i passed out in front of snakes, i got so lost i had to restart and google a map, thank goodness for those people or i dont think i would have finished this masterpiece of a survival game. this is by far the most survivally survival game out there. I bought this game on sale for like $3. I would not recommend spending more than that. The map is extremely frustrating, so you spend a lot of time wandering aimlessly. Also "open world survival craft" as this game's genre is a bit misleading. You have to constantly move in story mode, so it would be useless to build a base anywhere. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the map exploration as challenging due to the lack of an in-game marker showing the player's current location and the need to collect physical map pieces.

citations.review_text:
Green Hell is a solid survival game that leans more heavily on the survival mechanics over outright combat. You have to balance 3 food groups as well as water, so eating the same thing over and over will not give you a full health bar. The drain on hunger and thirst is pretty severe, so I would not recommend playing on the difficulties that just increase their depletion. At first it's pretty hard to meet your food needs but once you find a few good sources it becomes pretty easy. The medical stuff can also be pretty complicated, but it becomes satisfying once the pieces start to click. Honestly in early game you might want to consult the wiki here and there to mitigate some frustration.

The base building is pretty simple and limited compared to some other games, but it's good enough. The game encourages you more to live on the move as you have to do a lot of exploring for the story. Exploration can be hard as you have to collect pieces of the map and there is no GPS, and at time very little landmarks. If you get lost easily you'll have a bad time.

The story is pretty basic; much like The Forest games it feels like the story is secondary to the gameplay, it's not bad or anything but it's meant to just be serviceable.

Overall I would recommend it if you're into this kind of game, but probably not if you're not into survival stuff. I think Sons of the Forest strikes a better balance of atmosphere, action, survival, and difficulty, but this is a little bit of a different flavor that's worth trying. It also shines as a co-op game, solo can be very tedious with resource gathering and whatnot.

citations.review_text: Really fun game which is a true rival to The Forest! The voices made me want to see a doctor though as I honestly thought I was hearing things.
great game just turn off the sanity filter otherwise you will hear voices saying kill yourself

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs and synchronization issues in co-op sessions, such as progress not saving properly between sessions and items disappearing or not rendering when thrown between players.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to thoroughly enjoy this game, but some of the bugs most prominent in co-op meant I just had to put it down. The person I played with would save, only for us to load in during the next session and all of that progress to not have been saved properly, forcing us to re-do things, this was especially rough after a very long and productive session. 

It is a lot of fun, the learning curve is rough but you feel so accomplished once you work things out... But the loss of hard won progress really did just kill it.

Much like most of this companies games, it's more stable in solo player but more fun with friends, just be prepared for redoing things if you have the patience.

This game has an interesting story, but the multiplayer is terrible, sync problems left and right, save and spawn points ignored, NPCs showing up for one player but not for another, constant disconnects and objects missing or not being seen when one player throws it on the ground to another.
It's a pity as this is a nice game, but for multiplayer is a disappointment.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from crashes and lacks an auto-save feature, which can result in losing hours of gameplay progress.

citations.review_text:
This game is conceptually great but is lacking in a few key areas.
Difficulty is easy once you learn the mechanics. Tribesman lack realistic AI and will ignore their buddies being headshot from a distance in camp. Building can be a pain as it often won't let you place things that you would think you have the room for.
Main story was pretty linear but worth the playthrough. The prequel story however, is a mess of a grind and feels like work after a short while. 
Ran into two game breaking bugs. First was getting stuck with no way out except to die of thirst. Second bug was brutal with the game crashing after a cut scene, losing over two hours of work towards finally finishing Spirits of Amazonia story.

Still crashes on me all the time, which is a bit of a shame for a title that has been out of early access for so long. Combine that with a lack of auto save features and you got yourself a ruined evening. 

The game is fun when it doesn't though,
...although it's pretty punishing if you don't know already what you're doing. It's supposed to be "realistically hard", and in some ways it succeeds with that while failing in others. The game teaches you its mechanics very clumsily through failure and the PC's voice lines. If you're playing with a group of newbies that works best imo, you just keep failing and eventually figure ♥♥♥♥ out. 
If you're playing alone or you're the only new guy you should either be tolerant to frustration or not mind looking some things up. 

Either way, it was fun for me (mainly because of the gut punch of a story), but I'll not come back. The crashes are just too annoying imo. 

(Playing on Windows 11, Ryzen 7000 series CPU, RX 7000 series GPU, tons of RAM. This is not my PC's fault.)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as very difficult for beginners, requiring external guides or tutorials to understand crafting recipes and survival systems.

citations.review_text:
I played this game for 30 hours completely unable to find the plot (wandered my way all the way to the last zone) before I realized I had accidentally started on "Survival" mode which turned off the story. I started again and went through everything properly and it's a pretty rough experience. 

+ Fairly immersive survival experience with lots to explore
+ Survival on higher difficulties is challenging
+ Items you create have a great progression system

- Pretty much impossible to play without looking things up. If you like going into a game blind, this game is not for you. A lot of the crafting is unintuitive and not knowing certain recipes is pretty much a guarantee of a slow boring death. The worst offenders are dealing with Infections and venomous bites whose effects are very deadly if you don't know the one or two possible cures... very few of which are intuitive and none of them are hinted at in any way in gameplay. 
- The Main story has you move so fast that building a base is out of the question. Spirits of Amazonia fixes this but SoA is a horrible grind with a million objectives you have to find, all of which are spread throughout the dense jungle and require either using a guide/online map or randomly exploring for 50 hours to find everything. 
- Construction is somehow even slower than The Forest. Building a forward base camp when exploring a new place is a long endeavor, mostly due to the low carrying capacity and frustration with gathering logs and long sticks from trees that mostly just drop sticks. Bamboo is much nicer to build with but not as common and the smaller "stick" ones never respawn. Most notably everything needs ropes. Building anything feels like a rope-gathering simulator. Building a house large enough to have all the game's structures in it took 30 in-game days.

Really tough game when you start, trying to get familiar with the controls and environment at once, I found it  best to watch a couple of beginner guides to get started. The crafting is great with lots to craft , weapons armour , tools,  storage, pottery, furniture, etc.  there are  a few crops to plant and grow. The base building is awesome with Treehouse builds, floating houses and  ground based building.

100% the game after 100 hours. My favorite survival game and here's why. 
 
1) The story
For a survival game, it actually has a believable and interesting premise. I don't really beeline my way through survival storylines since I enjoy the exploration and gameplay loop more, but the ending did feel rewarding and had twists that surprised me with its direction.

2) The realism
Kinda reminds me of the long dark in regards to the fact that you have to worry about nutrition and water needs. Your main enemy is the effects of the environment and predators. The game is extremely difficult when you first start. Once you know what you're doing though, you find optimal ways to fulfill your needs and keep yourself healthy while you explore. 

3) The map
This game is beautiful. The map is pretty large (especially once you beat the main story and begin Spirits of Amazonia) and if you have a capable PC I bet the graphics look incredible on max. Honestly enough said. It's gorgeous.

What are the cons? As much as I enjoy this game I will be the first to admit that -- like most other survival games -- it gets repetitive. After you learn the mechanics you may fall into a gameplay loop of hunting  and gathering the same few things. This is mitigated by the nutritional system, which means you can't just eat one thing, but instead you need to eat two or three of the same thing and you'll be fine. 

Also, the building and resource gathering can be boring. Carrying sticks and wood like a drone just to build a fence or whatever is not something I enjoy. I built the bare minimum usually and just did my own thing. 

Lastly, the combat. Unfortunately, the best way to do ANYTHING in this game is to use a bow. If you're not using a bow you're crippling yourself. once you realize you can kill an entire camp of tribesman with like 5 arrows and semi-decent aim, you stop being threatened by anything. 

That's about it. It's fun though, and this game goes on sale for like $2 a couple times a year wh…
